items.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my uncle - his name is Andres Guerra Cardenas - was the one who taught me to play the bongos.

ctx.x: Tell us some of your fond memories of your parents and your childhood.

Well when I was four, my uncle - his name is Andres Guerra Cardenas - was the one who taught me to play the bongos. The way I learned to play the bongos - I was four years old - was with two empty cans of milk. My uncle made me repeat what he played on the bongos. He’d make me repeat what I heard him play and I’d repeat it on the empty condensed milk cans and that was my first inspiration. That gave me inspiration to continue learning aside from the fact that I was in school, too. I was still in Kindergarten. But…
Was your uncle a professional musician?
